newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha weaker, buyers scarce, arb East closing.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha weaker, buyers scarce, arb East closing.

text.p: European naphtha prices weakened on Wednesday with scarce buyers forcing sales at lower prices and with eastern arbitrage options closing as recent shipments from Europe start to pressure prices there, traders said.

Around 400,000 tonnes is estimated to have sailed East from Europe, around half of this has been taken up by short covering into increased petrochemical demand while the balance remains unsold and is starting to pressure prices in Asia.

Asian prices were valued around $230 a tonne on Monday but had already shed around $6 by this morning. Traders said that with relatively expensive freight at around $30 a tonne the arbitrage was no longer profitable.
Trader selling saw open spec offered down to around $191 cif NWE with a small 10kt parcel traded at the level on Tuesday.
Despite slack gasoline activity some interest was seen for N+A material into the U.K. with a cargo reported traded on Tuesday at mean of cif quotes -$1 per tonne.
In the Mediterranean several stems were being shown by trade houses, but traders said the dearth of buying interest at the moment meant levels were hard to pin down.
